run.final_report:
# Research Report

## Executive Summary
PostgreSQL and MySQL both provide JSON capabilities but differ in JSON implementation details and licensing.

## Research Question
Compare PostgreSQL and MySQL for JSON support and licensing.

## Methodology
Compared collected PostgreSQL and MySQL sources.

## Key Findings
- PostgreSQL supports JSON and JSONB.
- PostgreSQL uses the PostgreSQL License.
- MySQL supports a native JSON data type.
- MySQL Community Edition is available under GPL licensing.

## Comparison / Analysis
Both systems support JSON; the gathered evidence also records different licensing terms.

## Limitations
- Performance was outside this task.

## Sources
- PostgreSQL JSON Types (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-json.html)
- MySQL Licensing (https://www.mysql.com/about/legal/licensing/oem/)

# Research Report

## Executive Summary
ExampleCloud Pro costs $10 more per month than Basic, a $120 annual difference.

## Research Question
Compare ExampleCloud Basic and Pro pricing and calculate the annual difference.

## Methodology
Used pricing evidence and a calculator step over two research iterations.

## Key Findings
- Basic costs $10 per month.
- Pro costs $20 per month.
- The annual price difference is $120.

## Comparison / Analysis
Pro is $10 more per month, which produces a $120 annual difference.

## Limitations
- Taxes and discounts were not evaluated.

## Sources
- ExampleCloud Pricing (https://example.com/pricing)
